Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 26-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  FIFTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  Fundamentals of Machine Learning [CSE_3127]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                     Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                You are given a dataset with overlapping classes where hard-margin SVM fails to converge. After       (5)  
  applying soft-margin SVM with different C values (C = 0.01, C = 1, C = 100), you observe varying  
  A)           performance on training and test sets.  
  (i) With the help of neat diagrams, illustrate how the margin width, support vectors, and  
  misclassified points.  
  Then, analyze how the choice of C affects the number of support vectors, margin width, and  
  classification errors.  
  (ii) Using the bias-variance decomposition framework, analyse why extremely small and extremely  
  large C values both lead to poor generalization. Support your analysis with reasoning about  
  underfitting and overfitting.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           With the help of a diagram, explain the Stacking ensemble approach along with its major steps.        (3)  
  Analyse how the meta-model in stacking improves prediction accuracy by combining strong  
  learners. Explain the working of Bagging (Bootstrap Aggregation) with the help of a neat diagram  
  and the main steps involved.  
  Analyse how Bagging reduces variance and improves model stability.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)                                                                                                                 (2)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                Evaluate how pre-pruning and post-pruning techniques affect the generalization performance of a       (4)  
  decision tree. Using the principle of cost-complexity pruning, analyse the trade-off between model  
  A)           simplicity and accuracy.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           List the steps of the XGBoost algorithm. Analyse how learning from residuals differs from             (3)  
  AdaBoost's weight-based approach.  
  
  Page #1

Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)   Analyse the model complexity versus error curve and explain how changes in model complexity               (3)  
  influence training and test errors. Identify the region corresponding to underfitting, overfitting, and  
  the optimal generalization point.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)        You are given the following training data:                                                                (4)  
  
  
  A)  
  
  
  Predict the flower type for a new flower with PetalSize = Medium and Color = Yellow. Apply the  
  Naïve Bayes classifier to find the most probable FlowerType.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)   In noisy or non-separable datasets, the Perceptron learning algorithm keeps updating the                  (3)  
  hyperplane indefinitely. Analyze why this happens and how introducing a margin (e.g. in case of  
  SVM) could mitigate the issue.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)                                                                                                             (3)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)        You are classifying drones based on their Speed (km/h) and Battery Endurance (hours) to predict           (5)  
  the mission type they are best suited for.  
  A)  
  
  
  Page #2

Two test drones are observed:  
  
  1. T₁ = (7.5, 5.0)  
  2. T₂ = (9.0, 3.0)  
  
  Apply the k-NN classification algorithm with Euclidean distance and k = 3 to predict the mission type  
  for both test drones. Show all distance calculations and the final class for T₁ and T₂.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)         Analyse how problem-transformation methods (such as Binary Relevance or Classifier Chains)              (3)  
  differ in capturing inter-label dependencies, and the structural reason behind their performance  
  differences.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)         Analyse how the Linear Kernel, Polynomial Kernel, and RBF Kernel differ in terms of their ability to    (2)  
  handle non-linear decision boundaries.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)              Analyze how introducing a time-decay function in Timed PageRank modifies the random-surfer              (4)  
  model of traditional PageRank, and examine the key steps of the Timed PageRank algorithm.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO6" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)         Analyse how Content-Based Filtering builds user profiles using item feature vectors such as TF-IDF (3)  
  representations.  
  Explain Content-Based Filtering and how this approach helps mitigate the cold-start problem for new  
  users but struggles with over-specialization.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO6" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)         Analyse how Co-Citation helps in identifying the similarity between two documents.                      (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO6" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"
